description:
Wide Horizons

Required · LunaLib and GraphicsLib

Description

Important: v1.5.x is Not Save-Compatible with older version 1.4.x

Wide Horizons lets you decide how far apart the stars are, how much there is to find, and how expensive it is to travel.
You can keep the familiar Core Worlds close together, spread them across a larger map, or make the frontier denser without stretching every trip.

Wide Horizons (Core)
Enable Wide Horizons in the launcher.
Sector generation, exploration and travel settings, system discovery, and hyperspace music.
Wide Horizons + Content (WIP)
Enable Wide Horizons and Wide Horizons - Content in the launcher.
Everything in Core plus Dark Stars, Strange Hyperspace, story missions, and EidolON encounters.

What Core adds

Choose the shape of your sector
Scaling Mode changes the width and height of the sector, from 50% to 300% of the original dimensions. Leave constellation count on Auto with automatic scaling enabled to add more groups of star systems as the map grows. Choose a fixed count if you want a wide, sparsely populated frontier.
Performance Mode fits more star systems and exploration sites into a map that grows more gradually. The percentages here are presets for how much the sector contains. For a first run, try the 125% or 150% preset.
Core World Scale lets you decide how far apart the inhabited Core Worlds are. Choose Vanilla to keep the Core's original scale while expanding the frontier.
Randomize Sector Layout is an experimental option that shuffles most system positions while keeping each faction's inhabited systems grouped together. Systems with fixed positions are excluded.

Explore more varied star systems
Realistic system generation builds uninhabited, randomly generated systems around the type and age of their stars. Look for hot rocky worlds close in, ice worlds farther out, and occasional habitable worlds at more suitable distances. Gas giants can have rings and moons, and a rare planet can turn up far from the rest of the system.
Vanilla generation is available if you prefer Starsector's usual mix of planets and orbits in random systems. Handcrafted systems and inhabited worlds keep their existing planets.
More places to salvage and survey can include ruins, Domain probes, survey ships, research stations, cryosleepers, mothership chains, and Coronal Taps. Tune how common these sites are and how often Remnant territory is heavily defended.
Optional system discovery lets you hide eligible systems from the map until your fleet detects a way in. You can also enable discovery messages and Intel entries for warning beacons.

Tune travel, salvage, and hyperspace
Travel costs and deadlines can be adjusted for a larger sector. Reduce fuel use and day-to-day supply consumption, or give supported missions more time for longer trips. Repairs and combat readiness recovery still use their usual supplies.
Hyperspace conditions are adjustable. Set cloud density and gate frequency, change how far the Abyss reaches at the sector's edge, or turn off storms and slipstreams.
Map and music options let you hide the decorative nebula clouds in Starscape and toggle Wide Horizons' hyperspace tracks.
Salvage rewards let you adjust rare blueprint and hullmod finds separately from fuel and supplies. Set these options from the main menu before loading or starting a campaign.

What the Content add-on adds

Dark Stars are hidden systems reached through unusual rifts. Void Stars bend light and interfere with readings. Pulse Stars send out bursts of radiation. Search the surrounding anomalies for probes, wreckage, and abandoned stations.
Strange Hyperspace spreads outward from anomalies over time. Affected areas can interfere with sensors and make travel hazardous. A LunaSettings option limits further spread while leaving affected areas in place.
A three-part investigation starts with a chance encounter in a bar. Follow an unusual piece of technology through a Tri-Tachyon investigation into the source of the anomalies.
EidolON technology and encounters give the investigation some teeth. You can face mirror fleets, recover unusual salvage, and find technology that can be put to work at a colony.
Black Project is an optional campaign start about a covert operation beyond the Core. You can begin allied with the United Aurora Federation or stay independent with high UAF standing. This start requires Nexerelin and United Aurora Federation.

Screenshots
Spoiler

Compatibility & Tested Mods

Survival Mode · Derelict ship finds follow Survival Mode's recovery and ship-condition rules.
Nexerelin · Optional for regular campaigns. When Nexerelin's random sector option is active, it takes priority over Wide Horizons' own random layout option.
Customizable Star Systems · Wide Horizons can place and scale systems created with Customizable Star Systems.

If your custom system stays in the wrong place, give its first star an explicit name or set the system's location in its configuration so Wide Horizons can identify it.

Patchnotes
Spoiler
Version 1.5.0 (November 2026)

Not Save compatible with 1.4.x

IMPORTANT: Please reset the settings when starting a new game, as some values have changed to their default settings

Modified:
Migrated Wide Horizons to Java 17
Split Wide Horizons into Core and an optional Content module
Core includes sector generation and scaling and can be used on its own
Content requires Core and adds missions, Dark Star systems, and Eidolon content
Removed the countdown from the third Strange Hyperspace mission, which has no time limit

Fixed:
Sector generation no longer stalls if derelict probes or survey ships cannot be placed
Fixed hyperspace terrain clearing around fixed star systems when scaling the sector
The research team now waits for the decoder before starting its analysis and delivers the results only once
The follow-up contact now verifies that the correct market is still available
The final briefing can be retried if the decoder could not be awarded
Salvage bonuses now update when scaling settings change
Disabling fuel scaling clears leftover fuel modifiers from Wide Horizons
Loading a campaign now restores missing scripts that keep campaign bonuses up to date
Eidolon Server Hub bonuses now pause during construction or disruption
Duplicate AI cores no longer stack their bonuses
The salvage reset command now clears Wide Horizons bonuses from both the fleet and the player while preserving bonuses from other mods

Note:
I'm counting on your feedback to help me adjust the default settings for the current system sizes.
GitHub releases · Older changelog

Feedback & Support

This is my first mod for Starsector please don't be so hard on me if there are any problems.
For Discord support, please contact me at Taiwendo
Post your feedback or questions below!
Happy exploring,
- Taiwendo -

Note on Content Creation:
Java Code: I wrote this myself with the help of a friend who has more experience with Java.
Graphics: The graphics have been enhanced with AI but were not generated entirely by AI. Some of these graphics are still partially placeholders.
Music: Created by me in "Ableton"
